### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you passionate about protecting human health and the environment from hazardous substances, and restoring contaminated properties to beneficial use, especially in environmental justice communities? This is an opportunity to join DTSC’s team of professionals who work toward these goals. Join us today!

**As a Supervising Toxicologist you will have the opportunity to:**

* Manage and supervise administrative staff and subordinate toxicologists responsible for the human health risk evaluation and cleanup of hazardous waste contaminated properties
* Ensure that SMRP decisions are technically sound, innovative, consistent with DTSC goals and procedures, and protective of public health and the environment
* Provide staff with support, expertise, resources, and training to make appropriate project decisions in an effective and efficient matter
* Identify and procure adequate levels of resources necessary to meet staff recruitment efforts, staff development, and performance measures as outlined in the DTSC Strategic Plan
* Advise and consult with the Division Chiefs, Deputy Director, and Director with respect to policy issues associated with SMRP and respond to requests from Cal/EPA, the Governor’s Office, the Legislature, environmental and related stakeholder groups, and public regarding cleanup issues
* Identifies appropriate long-range plans and goals to address succession planning and knowledge transfer

jobs.description:
**Job Overview:**

APTIM is currently seeking an **Environmental Scientist/Geologist** in California for our Solid Waste Services Group in the Concord CA area to support our exciting portfolio of projects. We provide the following services to both the public and private sectors:

* Environmental compliance for solid waste sites,
* Landfill gas collection and control system (GCCS) design and operations and maintenance,
* Construction quality assurance,
* Solid Waste Reporting for site-specific and General Waste Discharge Requirements,
* Environmental site assessments and remediation.

Our philosophy centers on developing and maintaining a culture of mutual respect and honesty, where people listen generously and speak straight. At APTIM, you can expect countless opportunities to learn, develop business and leadership skills, and engage on a multitude of projects.

**Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities:**

* Leading teams or projects
* Preparing site and grading plans, GCCS design, pump and piping plans, and conceptual layouts for solid waste projects
* Conduct field inspections and construction quality assurance (CQA) oversight
* Leading and completing regulatory compliance reports, work plans, and special studies
* Anticipating client needs and identifying solutions
* Utilizing skills and knowledge to solve complex problems
* Preparing and managing, scopes, budgets and schedules
* Coordinating with contractors and clients
* Collaborating with other team members
* Attending client meetings
* Providing other duties as required.
* Work may periodically involve oversight during the installation of monitoring wells and supervising other field tasks
* Communication of technical concepts, evaluation results, plans, reports, etc. during work team meetings; ensures conformance to applicable technical standards as well as company policies and procedures

**Basic Qualifications:**

* BS/MS Geology, Engineering, or related field
* 3-8 years of Landfill / Solid Waste experience
* Experience with collecting environmental field data including groundwater, surface water, leachate, and landfill gas
* Ability to work on multidisciplinary projects
* Excellent oral & written communication skills
* Ability to work in a team environment
* Self-starter and problem solver
* Excellent organizational skills
* Knowledge of federal and state environmental regulations
* Ability to wear proper PPE for work on hazardous waste sites
* Possess a "Safety First" work ethic

**About APTIM**

APTIM enhances the quality of the environment, wellbeing of people, resilience of communities, and opportunity for employees to make a difference, not just a living. A leading professional solutions firm, we specialize in environmental, sustainability, resilience, and infrastructure solutions. Our team of experts provide these integrated solutions for forward-thinking government agencies, commercial and industrial clients, and energy customers. Together, we create sustainable and resilient communities for all.

What you can expect from APTIM:

* Work that is worthy of your time and talent
* Respect and flexibility to live a full life at work and at home
* Dogged determination to deliver for our clients and communities
* A voice in making our company better
* Investment into your personal and professional development

As of the date of this posting, a good faith estimate of the current pay range for this position is $89,440 - $101,920 . Compensation depends on several factors including: experience, education, key skills, geographic location of the position, client requirements, external market competitiveness, and internal equity among other employees within APTIM.

**Employee Benefits**

APTIM Environmental Services is committed to providing an extensive range of benefits that protect and promote the health and financial well-being of our employees and their families through the APTIM Benefits Marketplace https://aptim.makeityoursource.com/.

* Medical, vision, and dental insurance: Through the marketplace, our employees can choose benefits from five metallic levels and 10+ carriers to find the right benefits that work for them in their location.
* Life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability insurance
* Paid holidays, vacation, and sick leave (eligibility based on company policy and applicable law)
* 401(k) APTIM offers three 401k plans through the Aon Pooled Employer Plan (PEP). The specific plan you are eligible for depends on the business unit you are in. The details of the largest plan are found here:
  + APTIM 401(k) Guide
  + APTIM - Helpful Documents

**About APTIM - In Pursuit of Better**

jobs.title: Junior Environmental Analyst
jobs.description:
Toeroek Associates is a dynamic small business provider of specialty consulting and analysis services to the U.S. Government. Our multi-disciplined environmental staff includes scientific, legal, and engineering experts who support federal and state government entities in compliance, remediation, field services, site assessments, oversight, historical and technical research, litigation, and community engagement. Toeroek offers a collaborative and congenial work environment with a team of passionate staff dedicated to finding solutions to complex problems in the fields of environment, records and knowledge management, and national security.

Toeroek Associates is seeking a junior-level Environmental Analyst to provide support in the Denver, Colorado, Sacramento, California, Dallas, Texas, or Chicago, Illinois areas.

**Summary**

The analyst will work as part of a team to assist EPA and other government agencies with administering environmental regulatory compliance and enforcement programs. Our focus is on cleaning up our communities. The analyst will work on multiple contracts, researching and compiling evidence to characterize contamination and identify potentially responsible parties (PRPs) at hazardous waste sites. Superior research, writing, and analytical skills are essential to this position, as is an interest in helping government agencies enforce their environmental regulations.

**Duties include:**

* Assist in identifying sources of information about PRP operations, including federal, state and local agencies, public libraries, private archives, and map and aerial photography archives
* Conduct research to obtain documents pertinent to PRP historical operations and waste disposal practices, as well as environmental regulatory compliance
* Review information on PRP operations, including responses to EPA information requests, facility inspection reports, sampling and investigation reports, hazardous materials inventories and other documents collected, and identify relevant data for purposes of analyzing Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) liability
* Draft evidence summary reports that present information about PRP operations, chemical usage, disposal practices, and soil and groundwater sampling data
* Review laboratory sampling data results for purposes of extracting and summarizing relevant data from sampling and investigation reports
* Review real property title documents and prepare title reports and tables showing the ownership history of the property
* Conduct corporate research and identify corporate successors (training will be provided)
* Input data and manage databases
* Translate information obtained from research into charts, graphs, maps, and infographics
* Occasional overnight travel may be required

**Education/Experience**

* Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Arts degree from an accredited university
* Minimum of two years of relevant work experience preferred

**Requirements**

* Hybrid arrangements for Lakewood, CO and Concord, CA.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Detailed, critical, and thoughtful writing and analysis skills
* Knowledge of or experience in environmental information collection, analysis, interpretation and report preparation
* Ability to function as a member of a team and work in a fast-paced environment
* Ability to handle multiple tasks at once and meet deadlines and to adapt quickly and smoothly to changing project requirements
* Proficient in Office 365 and Windows-based applications
* Ability to use software to retrieve, evaluate, and organize information and documents

**Bonus Skills/Certifications**

* Experience with ESRI suite of GIS software is a plus

This position's target hiring rate range is non-exempt, $21.63 to $25.48 per hour, DOQ. This is good faith and a reasonable estimate of the base compensation at the time of posting. Toeroek offers a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, Life, LTD, STD, and 401K.

Toeroek Associates, Inc. is an Equal Employment Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer.

*Toeroek Associates, Inc. maintains the policy of equal employment opportunity (EEO) shall apply to all terms, conditions, and privileges of employment, including hiring, testing, training and development, promotion, transfer, compensation, benefits, educational assistance, termination, layoffs, social and recreational programs, and retirement. Toeroek is committed to making employment decisions based on valid requirements, without regard to age, color, disability, gender identity, genetic information, military or veteran status, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or any other applicable status protected by state or local law.*

*Applicants with disabilities may contact Toeroek Associates, Inc., Human Resources via telephone, fax, e-mail, and other means to request and arrange for accommodations. If you need assistance to accommodate a disability, you may request an accommodation at any time. Please contact Human Resources at hr@toeroek.com.*

**WHO ARE WE?**  
San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)  
Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

**Our Mission:** To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

**Our Vision:** We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site at https://www.sfpuc.org/about-us/careers-sfpuc

**Why Join Us?**

This role offers a unique opportunity to help build and scale up critical water quality initiatives, combining technical analysis, project coordination, and field operations to protect public health across San Francisco and regional water systems. If you are passionate about water quality, regulatory compliance, large-scale infrastructure programs, and building efficient operational processes, we encourage you to apply!

 **Job Description**

**Project Name:** Hazard Assessment Program

**Project Description:**

Under the State of California’s new cross-connection control regulations, the SFPUC must review all service connections (~180,000+) to properties in San Francisco, as well as the eight other water systems under SFPUC’s control, to evaluate potential hazards to the public drinking water distribution system arising from activities on user premises. In addition, the new regulations require the installation of backflow prevention assemblies on about 4,200 fire service connections. SFPUC has submitted a plan to the State Water Resources Control Board with deadlines for completing hazard assessments by 2049, ensuring backflow prevention assemblies on all dedicated fire services by 2044.

**Position Summary**

Are you a technical professional looking to make a direct impact on public health and water safety on a massive scale? We are seeking a dynamic Utility Specialist to serve as the Technical Program Coordinator for our Water Quality Cross Connection Control (CCC) Program under the direction of the Hazard Assessments Program Manager.

In this vital role, you will contribute to the implementation of SFPUC Cross-Connection Control Program inline with new regulatory requirements established by the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) through the Cross Connection Control Policy Handbook (CCCPH).

You will help shape a high-profile, multi-decade program by developing tracking systems, operational processes, coordinating complex field logistics, and partnering with internal teams, contractors, and external stakeholders across multiple program areas including Hazard Assessments, Fire services upgrades and Regional Compliance.

**Work Location:** 1657 Rollins Road, Burlingame, CA, 94010

**Schedule:** Full-time, Monday – Friday

* This position requires a valid driver’s license.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* **Program Implementation & Compliance:** Develop and implement coordination protocols, workflows, and documentation processes for the CCC Program in compliance with SWRCB CCCPH requirements.
* **Systems & Data Management:** Establish tracking systems, dashboards, and reporting templates to monitor inspections, costs, schedules, and compliance metrics.
* **Research & Analysis:** Conduct research using internal databases, GIS systems, spreadsheets, field reports, and photos to compile baseline data on service connection characteristics and assess cross-connection hazards.
* **Cross-Functional Coordination:** Coordinate daily program activities with field staff, contractors, customers, and other City departments, serving as a liaison to ensure smooth communication, scheduling, and execution.
* **Contractor & Consultant Oversight:** Coordinate with contractors and consultants to ensure field activities align with approved scopes of work, schedules, and Cross Connection Control program requirements.
* **Reporting & Continuous Improvement:** Prepare program reports, dashboards, and documentation for Program Manager review, highlighting trends, risks, and lessons learned while developing procedures, reference materials, and recommendations to improve program effectiveness.
* **Field Engagement:** Conduct field coordination and site visits (as needed) to support hazard assessments, inspection activities, and validation of program data.
* **Technical Support:** Provide technical support for Hazard Assessment Program initiatives, including compliance studies, analytical tasks, and administrative support. Performs other project-related duties as assigned.

### **Job Description and Duties**

The mission of the Wildlife Diversity Program is to conserve the rich diversity of California's native wildlife, which includes tens of thousands of terrestrial invertebrates and more than 1,000 species of mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians. The program coordinates statewide conservation activities for native wildlife, including those designated as threatened or endangered pursuant to the California Endangered Species Act.

The Wildlife Diversity Program is hiring one California Endangered Species Act (CESA) Specialist! The incumbent will work independently and as part of a team to provide high level scientific, technical, and policy expertise to support the conservation, management, and monitoring of wildlife species listed under CESA. In this role, the incumbent will lead complex scientific analyses to support emergency listings and provisional candidate determinations under CESA, as well as CESA listing petitions, status reviews, five-year species reviews, recovery planning efforts, and scientific, educational, and management permitting. The incumbent will also support native wildlife conservation through a variety of program efforts which may include analyzing and synthesizing data, developing regulations, reviewing research permits, and developing grant proposals.

jobs.description:
For over 25 years, **dicentra** has been a trusted global leader in regulatory consulting and clinical research for the life sciences and dietary supplement industries. We partner with innovators worldwide to navigate complex regulatory landscapes, turn scientific rigor into commercial success, and bring safe, compliant products to market.

To support our continued growth and meet high client demand, we have an **immediate opening** for an experienced **Senior Regulatory Consultant / Toxicologist (GRAS & NDI Expert)** to join our dynamic, fully remote consulting team.

**The Opportunity**

In this senior-level role, you will serve as a premier technical authority and trusted advisor to our clients. You will lead scientific safety assessments, evaluate manufacturing chemistry, author high-impact regulatory submissions, and provide strategic roadmaps for novel food and dietary ingredients across both **human and veterinary applications**.

You will bridge the gap between complex science, rigorous toxicology, and commercial market access—helping clients determine the optimal regulatory pathways while delivering exceptional consulting service.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Regulatory Pathway Strategy & Feasibility:** Conduct feasibility assessments and gap analyses to determine whether novel ingredients require a GRAS (Generally Recognized as Safe) notification, an NDI (New Dietary Ingredient) notification, or alternative pathways.
* **Toxicology & Safety Evaluation:** Critically evaluate published and unpublished toxicology, safety, and efficacy data; design testing cascades and safety profiles to support ingredient safety determinations.
* **Manufacturing & Chemistry Assessment:** Review and assess detailed manufacturing processes, batch analyses, specifications, impurity and contaminant profiles, and stability data to ensure data integrity for GRAS/NDI dossiers.
* **Dossier Preparation & Submission:** Lead the end-to-end authoring, review, and assembly of robust GRAS notices, independent GRAS determinations, and NDI notifications for submission to the U.S. FDA.
* **Expert Panel Coordination:** Identify, convene, and lead Independent GRAS Expert Panels—managing consensus statements and scientific dialogues through to completion.
* **Broader Food & Dietary Supplement Compliance:** Support clients with high-level regulatory compliance, including product classifications, claim substantiation dossiers, and label/ingredient reviews.
* **Client Advisory & Account Leadership:** Act as a strategic partner to C-suite and R&D leaders, translating complex toxicology and FDA feedback into actionable business strategies.
* **Cross-Sector Scope:** Support regulatory strategies for both human food/supplements and animal/veterinary feed and ingredient submissions.

**Qualifications & Background**

* **Advanced Scientific Degree:** Ph.D. or Master’s in Toxicology, Pharmacology, Food Science, Biochemistry, or a closely related discipline (DABT certification is a strong asset).
* **Prior FDA Experience Strongly Preferred:** Direct experience working within the U.S. FDA (e.g., CFSAN or CVM) reviewing or evaluating GRAS, NDI, or food additive petitions.
* **Deep GRAS & NDI Mastery:** Proven track record authoring and successfully submitting GRAS determinations and NDI notifications with documented FDA engagement.
* **Manufacturing & Toxicological Acumen:** Strong familiarity with manufacturing flow charts, specs, and contaminant thresholds, paired with extensive experience evaluating genotoxicity, subchronic/chronic toxicity studies, safety margins, and ADME profiles.
* **Client-Facing Leadership:** Exceptional communication skills with the poise and commercial mindset required to manage client relationships and guide them through strategic decision-making.
* **Compliance Knowledge (Big Plus):** Demonstrated familiarity with U.S. dietary supplement and conventional food regulations, including 21 CFR Part 111, labeling compliance, and structure/function claim substantiation.

**Why Join dicentra?**

* **Fully Remote Flexibility:** Work from anywhere with a high degree of autonomy and collaborative virtual infrastructure.
* **Industry Leadership:** Join a recognized firm with a 25-year legacy of excellence and trust in life sciences and regulatory compliance.
* **High-Impact Work:** Direct involvement in shaping the market introduction of cutting-edge ingredients and formulations.
* **Dynamic Culture:** Collaborate with a multi-disciplinary team of passionate regulatory affairs experts, toxicologists, and clinical scientists who value innovation, excellence, and teamwork.

**How to Apply**

This position is **available to fill immediately**.

*We nourish an environment devoted to honesty and fairness, trust and respect. We care deeply for our team members and take work-life balance seriously, allowing our people to decide on a schedule that best fits their life and working preferences.*

**Best people**
  
*We unite cross-industry professionals with a shared passion for improving people’s health and wellness. Our inspiring leaders are accessible and work eagerly side-by-side with individual employees to help them understand and achieve their objectives.*

**Best opportunities**
  
*We encourage our team members to continuously develop and enhance their skills and expertise. We recognize and reward courageous choices and innovative ideas that result in the growth of our people and company, and in the success of our clients.*

Toeroek Associates is a dynamic small business provider of specialty consulting and analysis services to the U.S. Government. Our multi-disciplined environmental staff includes scientific, legal, and engineering experts who support federal and state government entities in compliance, remediation, field services, site assessments, oversight, historical and technical research, litigation, and community engagement. Toeroek offers a collaborative and congenial work environment with a team of passionate staff dedicated to finding solutions to complex problems in the fields of environment, records and knowledge management, and national security.

Toeroek Associates is seeking a junior-level Environmental Analyst to provide support in the Denver, Colorado, Sacramento, California, Dallas, Texas, or Chicago, Illinois areas.

**Summary**

The analyst will work as part of a team to assist EPA and other government agencies with administering environmental regulatory compliance and enforcement programs. Our focus is on cleaning up our communities. The analyst will work on multiple contracts, researching and compiling evidence to characterize contamination and identify potentially responsible parties (PRPs) at hazardous waste sites. Superior research, writing, and analytical skills are essential to this position, as is an interest in helping government agencies enforce their environmental regulations.

**Duties include:**

* Assist in identifying sources of information about PRP operations, including federal, state and local agencies, public libraries, private archives, and map and aerial photography archives
* Conduct research to obtain documents pertinent to PRP historical operations and waste disposal practices, as well as environmental regulatory compliance
* Review information on PRP operations, including responses to EPA information requests, facility inspection reports, sampling and investigation reports, hazardous materials inventories and other documents collected, and identify relevant data for purposes of analyzing Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) liability
* Draft evidence summary reports that present information about PRP operations, chemical usage, disposal practices, and soil and groundwater sampling data
* Review laboratory sampling data results for purposes of extracting and summarizing relevant data from sampling and investigation reports
* Review real property title documents and prepare title reports and tables showing the ownership history of the property
* Conduct corporate research and identify corporate successors (training will be provided)
* Input data and manage databases
* Translate information obtained from research into charts, graphs, maps, and infographics
* Occasional overnight travel may be required

**Education/Experience**

* Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Arts degree from an accredited university
* Minimum of two years of relevant work experience preferred

**Requirements**

* Hybrid arrangements for Lakewood, CO and Concord, CA.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Detailed, critical, and thoughtful writing and analysis skills
* Knowledge of or experience in environmental information collection, analysis, interpretation and report preparation
* Ability to function as a member of a team and work in a fast-paced environment
* Ability to handle multiple tasks at once and meet deadlines and to adapt quickly and smoothly to changing project requirements
* Proficient in Office 365 and Windows-based applications
* Ability to use software to retrieve, evaluate, and organize information and documents

**Bonus Skills/Certifications**

* Experience with ESRI suite of GIS software is a plus

This position's target hiring rate range is non-exempt, $21.63 to $25.48 per hour, DOQ. This is good faith and a reasonable estimate of the base compensation at the time of posting. Toeroek offers a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, Life, LTD, STD, and 401K.

The mission of the Wildlife Diversity Program is to conserve the rich diversity of California's native wildlife, which includes tens of thousands of terrestrial invertebrates and more than 1,000 species of mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians. The program coordinates statewide conservation activities for native wildlife, including those designated as threatened or endangered pursuant to the California Endangered Species Act.

The Wildlife Diversity Program is hiring one California Endangered Species Act (CESA) Specialist! The incumbent will work independently and as part of a team to provide high level scientific, technical, and policy expertise to support the conservation, management, and monitoring of wildlife species listed under CESA. In this role, the incumbent will lead complex scientific analyses to support emergency listings and provisional candidate determinations under CESA, as well as CESA listing petitions, status reviews, five-year species reviews, recovery planning efforts, and scientific, educational, and management permitting. new_jobs.title: Senior Regulatory Consultant / Toxicologist – GRAS & NDI Expert
new_jobs.description:
For over 25 years, **dicentra** has been a trusted global leader in regulatory consulting and clinical research for the life sciences and dietary supplement industries. We partner with innovators worldwide to navigate complex regulatory landscapes, turn scientific rigor into commercial success, and bring safe, compliant products to market.

To support our continued growth and meet high client demand, we have an **immediate opening** for an experienced **Senior Regulatory Consultant / Toxicologist (GRAS & NDI Expert)** to join our dynamic, fully remote consulting team.

**The Opportunity**

In this senior-level role, you will serve as a premier technical authority and trusted advisor to our clients. You will lead scientific safety assessments, evaluate manufacturing chemistry, author high-impact regulatory submissions, and provide strategic roadmaps for novel food and dietary ingredients across both **human and veterinary applications**.

You will bridge the gap between complex science, rigorous toxicology, and commercial market access—helping clients determine the optimal regulatory pathways while delivering exceptional consulting service.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Regulatory Pathway Strategy & Feasibility:** Conduct feasibility assessments and gap analyses to determine whether novel ingredients require a GRAS (Generally Recognized as Safe) notification, an NDI (New Dietary Ingredient) notification, or alternative pathways.
* **Toxicology & Safety Evaluation:** Critically evaluate published and unpublished toxicology, safety, and efficacy data; design testing cascades and safety profiles to support ingredient safety determinations.
* **Manufacturing & Chemistry Assessment:** Review and assess detailed manufacturing processes, batch analyses, specifications, impurity and contaminant profiles, and stability data to ensure data integrity for GRAS/NDI dossiers.
* **Dossier Preparation & Submission:** Lead the end-to-end authoring, review, and assembly of robust GRAS notices, independent GRAS determinations, and NDI notifications for submission to the U.S. FDA.
* **Expert Panel Coordination:** Identify, convene, and lead Independent GRAS Expert Panels—managing consensus statements and scientific dialogues through to completion.
* **Broader Food & Dietary Supplement Compliance:** Support clients with high-level regulatory compliance, including product classifications, claim substantiation dossiers, and label/ingredient reviews.
* **Client Advisory & Account Leadership:** Act as a strategic partner to C-suite and R&D leaders, translating complex toxicology and FDA feedback into actionable business strategies.
* **Cross-Sector Scope:** Support regulatory strategies for both human food/supplements and animal/veterinary feed and ingredient submissions.

**Qualifications & Background**

* **Advanced Scientific Degree:** Ph.D. or Master’s in Toxicology, Pharmacology, Food Science, Biochemistry, or a closely related discipline (DABT certification is a strong asset).
* **Prior FDA Experience Strongly Preferred:** Direct experience working within the U.S. FDA (e.g., CFSAN or CVM) reviewing or evaluating GRAS, NDI, or food additive petitions.
* **Deep GRAS & NDI Mastery:** Proven track record authoring and successfully submitting GRAS determinations and NDI notifications with documented FDA engagement.
* **Manufacturing & Toxicological Acumen:** Strong familiarity with manufacturing flow charts, specs, and contaminant thresholds, paired with extensive experience evaluating genotoxicity, subchronic/chronic toxicity studies, safety margins, and ADME profiles.
* **Client-Facing Leadership:** Exceptional communication skills with the poise and commercial mindset required to manage client relationships and guide them through strategic decision-making.
* **Compliance Knowledge (Big Plus):** Demonstrated familiarity with U.S. dietary supplement and conventional food regulations, including 21 CFR Part 111, labeling compliance, and structure/function claim substantiation.

**Why Join dicentra?**

* **Fully Remote Flexibility:** Work from anywhere with a high degree of autonomy and collaborative virtual infrastructure.
* **Industry Leadership:** Join a recognized firm with a 25-year legacy of excellence and trust in life sciences and regulatory compliance.
* **High-Impact Work:** Direct involvement in shaping the market introduction of cutting-edge ingredients and formulations.
* **Dynamic Culture:** Collaborate with a multi-disciplinary team of passionate regulatory affairs experts, toxicologists, and clinical scientists who value innovation, excellence, and teamwork.

**How to Apply**

This position is **available to fill immediately**.

**Why join us**

**Best workplace**
  
*We nourish an environment devoted to honesty and fairness, trust and respect. We care deeply for our team members and take work-life balance seriously, allowing our people to decide on a schedule that best fits their life and working preferences.*

**Best people**
  
*We unite cross-industry professionals with a shared passion for improving people’s health and wellness. Our inspiring leaders are accessible and work eagerly side-by-side with individual employees to help them understand and achieve their objectives.*

**Best opportunities**
  
*We encourage our team members to continuously develop and enhance their skills and expertise. We recognize and reward courageous choices and innovative ideas that result in the growth of our people and company, and in the success of our clients.*

**Become a part of a purpose-driven and future-oriented business that impacts and improves millions of lives worldwide!**
